title: Animals with robust regeneration also resist cancer and aging

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Animals with robust regeneration also resist cancer and aging

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Animals with robust morphogenetic control due to high plasticity are resistant to perturbation at many scales: they regenerate lost limbs and organs, readily suppress cancer, and resist aging, contrary to the expectation that easy access to undifferentiated cells should make them highly cancer-prone.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Beginner’s mind: self-organization on the fly as the origin of multiscale competency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Animals with robust morphogenetic control due to high levels of plasticity are resistant to changes of circumstance (injury) at many scales: they regenerate after loss of limbs and organs (degradation of body-scale information), they suppress cancer readily [238] (degradation of tissue-scale information) and they resist aging (degradation of cell-level information).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Beginner’s mind: self-organization on the fly as the origin of multiscale competency”. Scope: Animals across taxa, especially highly regenerative ones such as planaria and salamanders

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public comparative longevity data exist, but cancer surveillance is dominated by humans and managed animals and regenerative capacity needs compilation. Existing data can test selected taxa, not the broad causal generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across taxa, quantify regenerative capacity, neoplasia incidence or tumor-suppression traits, and lifespan or senescence rates while controlling for body size, phylogeny, surveillance effort, and life history. A positive joint association supports the generalization; repeated high-regeneration taxa with high cancer or rapid aging refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Body size, lifespan, and phylogeny confound associations.

Cross-species cancer incidence is severely underobserved.

Regeneration and plasticity lack standardized comparative scores.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.7
data existence: 0.75
analysis feasibility: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Longevity is tabulated for many species, so the aging arm has a real dataset, while regeneration and cancer resistance are scattered qualitative reports. A phylogenetically controlled test can be sketched for a subset of taxa and would be informative only with serious confounds. The expectation about undifferentiated cells and cancer is not a separate measured variable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rank species by an explicit regeneration score, a cancer-incidence measure, and a longevity measure, then test whether high regeneration predicts low cancer and long life after phylogenetic correction. A joint association in that direction would support the comparative pattern; regenerative taxa with high cancer or short life, or a pattern that vanishes under phylogeny and body size, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Regeneration ability and comparative cancer rates are not in one open table and are biased by how hard tumors are to see in small aquatic animals.

Body size, phylogeny, and indeterminate growth confound any three-way association.
